summary: S-Amlodipine (levamlodipine) is the pharmacologically active S-enantiomer of amlodipine, a long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used for hypertension and chronic stable/vasospastic angina. Because the inactive R-enantiomer is removed, the S-form is given at roughly half the dose of racemic amlodipine and is claimed to cause less ankle edema. The usual dose is 2.5 mg once daily, up to 5 mg.
indications: Essential hypertension (alone or with other antihypertensives)
Off-label / regional: as an edema-sparing alternative to racemic amlodipine

dosage.d: Increase to 5 mg once daily as needed
Start 2.5 mg once daily and titrate slowly

admin: Take orally once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
Allow several days to a couple of weeks between dose increases (long half-life, gradual onset)
Start at the lower dose in the elderly and in hepatic impairment
Do not stop abruptly in angina without medical advice
Monitor blood pressure and check for ankle swelling
moa: S-Amlodipine is the active S(-)-enantiomer of amlodipine. It inhibits the transmembrane influx of calcium ions into vascular smooth muscle and cardiac muscle through L-type calcium channels, preferentially relaxing peripheral and coronary arterial smooth muscle. This lowers peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure, and increases coronary blood flow, relieving angina. The inactive R-enantiomer of racemic amlodipine contributes little to vasodilation but is associated with edema.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to amlodipine or other dihydropyridines
Unstable angina (except vasospastic) / hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI
monitor: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers

preg: Limited human data. Use only if clearly needed; calcium channel blockers have been used in pregnancy but safety of the S-enantiomer specifically is not well established. Weigh benefit against risk.
lact: Amlodipine is excreted in human breast milk in small amounts; a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking account of its importance to the mother.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment; amlodipine is not dialyzable.
hepatic: Clearance is reduced and half-life prolonged in hepatic impairment. Initiate at the lowest dose and titrate slowly; use caution in severe impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - increase amlodipine exposure and hypotension risk
Simvastatin - limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day due to increased myopathy risk
moderate: Sildenafil and other PDE5 inhibitors - additive blood-pressure lowering
minor: Grapefruit juice - modest increase in exposure
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; large amounts of grapefruit may slightly raise levels.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect.

serious: Worsening angina or rare myocardial infarction on initiation/dose increase (especially severe CAD)

monitoring: Blood pressure (sitting/standing) at baseline and after dose changes
Liver function if hepatic symptoms develop
counsel: Take once daily at the same time; do not stop suddenly if used for angina
Rise slowly from sitting/lying to reduce dizziness
Report significant ankle swelling, severe dizziness or worsening chest pain
Effects build over days; full benefit may take a couple of weeks
pk: Plasma peak ~6-12 hours after oral dose
Store at room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not an FDA-approved product; S-amlodipine (levamlodipine) is marketed via SmPC/national approvals (e.g., India, parts of Asia/EU). Data largely extrapolated from racemic amlodipine and the active S-enantiomer
Given at roughly half the dose of racemic amlodipine (2.5 mg S-amlodipine ~ 5 mg amlodipine) because the inactive R-enantiomer is removed
Marketed claim of less ankle edema than racemic amlodipine; evidence is modest
Very long half-life means slow onset and offset - titrate gradually and do not expect rapid BP change
Limit simvastatin to 20 mg/day when co-prescribed (same as amlodipine)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose; then skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive peripheral vasodilation with marked, possibly prolonged, hypotension and reflex tachycardia. Treat with active cardiovascular support: place supine with elevated limbs, give IV fluids, vasopressors and IV calcium; consider further monitoring as effects are prolonged. Dialysis is not effective.
